mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE < 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly decline in real GDP growth (GDPC1) below 1% for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarterly growth < 1% for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 < 1% growth for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals a contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of six consecutive months of INDPRO below its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average, combined with a monthly decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL), signals improving housing demand with stable inflation, which boosts homebuilder and construction-related stocks and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average AND CPIAUCSL < previous month
regime_hint: improving housing demand with stable inflation
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST rises above its 12-month moving average and CPIAUCSL falls month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the federal funds rate below 3% for four consecutive months signals an extended monetary easing period, which lowers borrowing costs and supports corporate investment and consumer spending, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of four consecutive months with FEDFUNDS < 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in Real Personal Income (implied by RSAFS growth) above 0.5% while Industrial Production (INDPRO) grows below 0.2% for three consecutive months signals a demand-led expansion with weak supply response, which compresses profit margins and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > 0.5% AND INDPRO growth < 0.2% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS grows > 0.5% and INDPRO grows < 0.2% for three consecutive months.
